stances_toward.note: The former colony and still a main partner: a 2023-27 development programme of about EUR 50m a year, an ambassador who in Aug 2026 discussed an Umicore germanium project with a Belgian state guarantee with Tshisekedi, and a Belgian line that defends the DRC's territorial integrity against the M23 while urging an inclusive national dialogue. The wound is open: a Brussels court ruled on 17 Mar 2026 that Etienne Davignon will stand trial for the 1961 Lumumba killing. Bond - grievance (the colonial past).

stances_toward.note: Partner by minerals: the Sicomines minerals-for-infrastructure deal of 2008, renegotiated under Tshisekedi to USD 7bn of Chinese infrastructure (2024), Chinese companies (CMOC, Huayou, Chengtun, CNMC) running most of the cobalt mining in a country that produces over 70% of the world's supply, most of it shipped to China, a Belt and Road member since January 2021. Kinshasa's US minerals deal of 2025 is the hedge Beijing watches; the mines stay. Bond none.

stances_toward.note: Kinshasa agreed to Operation Shujaa with the UPDF from November 2021, so the two cooperate against the ADF out of necessity. Uganda resists alignment: the ICJ ordered it to pay USD 325m in reparations for its 1998-2003 occupation (judgment of 9 February 2022, payable in five USD 65m instalments; the first was paid in September 2022). Later instalments, due to 1 September 2026, are not verified. The UN experts say Ugandan units shielded M23 (July 2025 report as reported); Uganda denies it. reluctant_partner is our reading of that structure, not a source's word. Bond grievance: the ICJ case is an open wound. Gap: whether the 2026 instalments were paid.
